fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents present a credible transferable Node.js backend profile without manufacturing professional Python, FastAPI, Kafka, Kubernetes or database-tuning experience. Python and Terraform limitations are explicit, and ferry ticketing is framed as transport exposure rather than freight expertise. However, readiness to work mainly in Python is not explicitly stated, and safe database migrations, query tuning, API-scale performance and design documentation remain unproven. Backend code migration must not be mistaken for database schema-migration experience.

issues: The skills inventory and ten current-role bullets dilute the backend-focused narrative with substantial frontend and peripheral content.
The Sjöbris role heading is stranded at the bottom of page one, separated from its dates and all supporting bullets.
Arabic writing ability and current German proficiency are expressed slightly more positively than in the source.

reasons: Clean, single-column extracted text and standard headings make parsing straightforward.
The CV contains strong AWS, PostgreSQL, Docker, REST, testing, CI/CD and on-call matches.
Professional Python/FastAPI experience is absent and basic Python is explicitly personal-project experience.
Several missing keywords represent genuine gaps, not tailoring omissions.
An automated screen that insists on professional Python or the named event-streaming stack may reject this otherwise transferable profile.

issues: The third paragraph is long and combines the Python gap, observability, transport exposure, public speaking and English.
The production stack and testing/CI/CD experience are repeated across multiple paragraphs and the closing.
The Express-to-NestJS talk is mentioned twice in adjacent sentences.
'Technical lead for most of a React Native ferry-ticket application' awkwardly conflates project leadership with building most of the app.
The letter acknowledges the Python gap but does not explicitly say the candidate wants to work mainly in Python.
strengths: Correct employer, role and Routing & Tracking team; no stale agency-to-fintech application framing.
Uses the company's ownership culture and shipment-information purpose rather than generic praise.
Includes concrete conversion results, matching on-call cadence and relevant queue-based document processing.
Honestly distinguishes professional Node.js experience from personal Python projects.
Makes a restrained, defensible link between ferry ticketing and transport software.

culture_used: Engineering teams that own what they run

spacing_issues: The Sjöbris Developer heading appears alone at the foot of CV page one, while its 2018–2021 dates and bullets begin page two.
The CV's first page is dense, especially the technical-skills inventory and current-role bullet block.
The cover letter's third paragraph forms a visually heavy block; splitting it would improve scanning.
issues: Automated measurements report no problems, but the page images reveal the orphaned experience heading.
The serif typography, restrained rules and consistent body sizing look professional, though the CV could use stronger prioritisation.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'I was technical lead for most of a React Native ferry-ticket application' should distinguish 'project technical lead' from 'built most of the application'.
'I also shared what I learned ... in a talk' followed by 'I have explained technical decisions ... through my ... talk' repeats the same evidence unnecessarily.
The long sentence beginning 'My professional backend experience is primarily in Node.js and TypeScript rather than Python' repeats much of the preceding paragraph.

notes_facts_used: Frontend is the candidate's strongest area.
The maintained GraphQL BFF uses Apollo Server.
The candidate acted as team lead for four months in 2024, covering 1:1s and sprint planning without claiming a permanent title.

parsed.summary: The application is largely faithful and presents a credible Node.js/TypeScript engineer with relevant PostgreSQL, AWS, testing, delivery and on-call experience. It appropriately limits Python to personal projects and avoids inventing Kafka, Kubernetes or advanced Terraform expertise, although two language-proficiency descriptions are slightly softened. The main weaknesses are diffuse prioritisation, a repetitive cover-letter paragraph and the lack of an explicit commitment to working mainly in Python. The PDFs are readable and professional, but the Sjöbris role heading is orphaned across the CV page break. The visible conversation and final section order support compliance with the user's changed instructions, with intermediate edits not independently inspectable.
